why: not a QoS policy at all, despite the name. `rclc_deadline_policy_t` (RELEASED / ACTIVATED / INHERITED) is RFC-0047's real-time SCHEDULING deadline interpretation -- a field of `rclc_sched_context_t`, mirroring `nros_node::executor::sched_context::DeadlinePolicy`. The RTOS scenario is a periodic task whose deadline is measured from release, from activation, or inherited from its caller; rcl has no scheduling context so ROS 2 has nothing to compare it with. It appears in this stage because `topics.py`'s KEY_OVERRIDES maps `deadline_policy_t` to qos while its three siblings `sched_class_t`, `sched_priority_t` and `sched_context_t` map to exec -- the verdict is right, the shard is not.
